idea.title: Overly shallow
idea.summary: Kardas, Kumar and Epley 2022: strangers expected deep questions to be awkward, but deep chats felt closer and less awkward than predicted. Fresh angle: deep talk, not liking gap or commuters.
hookOptions: Deep questions with strangers aren't awkward
Scared to ask a stranger something real?
Researchers made strangers ask deep questions
Small talk is the awkward part
Strangers wanted shallow talk. They were wrong.
sources: Kardas, Kumar & Epley (2022), 'Overly shallow?', Journal of Personality and Social Psychology: strangers expected deeper conversations to be more awkward and less connecting than they were.

scenes.say: Deep questions with strangers feel awkward. Researchers say they're not.
In 2022, researchers paired up strangers and handed them deep questions.
Before talking, they guessed it would feel awkward.
They guessed wrong. The deep chats felt closer and less awkward.

scenes.name: Sunny Otter
scenes.label: Question one
scenes.say: So with your next stranger, skip the weather and ask the real thing.

scenes.ask: Your deep question for a stranger?
